My Battle of Algiers Summary
My Battle of Algiers by Ted Morgan
A Yale graduate who grew up in France and America, Ted Morgan was drafted into the French Army and served in Algeria in 1956 and 1957. In this memoir, the eminent historian and biographer relives the harrowing conflict in which everyone, French and Arab, became involved in unimaginable barbarities. Morgan himself beat and killed a prisoner who may have been responsible for the death of a friend.
Morgan lived through the day-to-day struggle to put down an Arab insurgency, with its unrelenting menu of bombings, assassinations and torture reminiscent of America's present difficulties in Iraq.
